newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus parliament renews bid to impeach Lukashenko.
newsitem.headline: Belarus parliament renews bid to impeach Lukashenko.

text.p: The Belarussian parliament began a fresh attempt to impeach hardline President Alexander Lukashenko on Saturday after the collapse of a compromise deal brokered by Russia.
Parliament speaker Semyon Sharetsky told a news conference he had signed a fresh request to impeach the president.
"I have signed the request about impeachment and sent it to the constitutional court. I have also withdrawn yesterday's request (to halt impeachment proceedings)," he said.

Impeachment proceedings were stopped after Friday's deal between Lukashenko and parliament, but the compromise collapsed on Saturday when deputies failed to approve it and Lukashenko said he was scrapping his side of the bargain.
Lukashenko wants to use a referendum set for Sunday to tighten his grip on rival institutions and extend his term by more than two years -- an idea fiercely opposed by parliament.

A delegation of parliamentary deputies arrived at the constitutional court on Saturday saying they had come to continue the impeachment proceedings against Lukashenko, who has been president since 1994.
"Parliament will not now withdraw impeachment proceedings because Lukashenko has annulled the agreement which was signed," deputy Alexander Dobrovolsky told Reuters as he arrived at the court.

Dobrovolsky said the deputies had collected more than the minimum 70 signatures necessary to restart the impeachment procedure. He accused Lukashenko of deliberately sabotaging the agreement with parliament.

A group of around 60 deputies out of 199 remain loyal to Lukashenko. If the constitutional court decides there is a case against the president, a two-thirds majority is required in parliament to remove him from office.
